_about: Independent reference values for scripts/fluid-gates/materials.mjs (S1.5). Printed values are copied from the cited documents; 'r4-derived' values are the plan's approved constants (FINAL-PLAN.md §4.2 / r4-materials-scale.md) and are checked at the precision they were printed with.

assael2012_table3_mercury_viscosity_mPa_.source: Assael et al. 2012, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 41, 033101, Table 3 (recommended values), liquid mercury, 3 decimals

bettin_fehlauer_2004_mercury_density_20C.source: Bettin & Fehlauer 2004, Metrologia 41 S16, reference value at 20 C, 101325 Pa (quoted in the Ayrinhac Hg compilation)

reading_glycerol_calculator_source_lines.source: Reading glycerol-water calculator (Cheng 2008 viscosity; Volk & Kahler 2018 density), JavaScript source, verbatim right-hand sides (T in C)

grd2008_table2_example.source: Giordano, Russell & Dingwell 2008, EPSL 271:123, Table 2: iron-free andesite melt with 2.00 wt% H2O; printed B = 7720, C = 334, log eta(1273 K) = 3.67

halverson_whittington_2024.source: Halverson & Whittington 2024, Geology 53:135 (NSF PAR manuscript): 'average viscosities of 116 Pa s at 1150 C' (line 34); Table 1 vesicularity: zero-time sample (quenched after the 20-min 1175 C hold that starts every run, lines 89-93) 36.1 %, recovered 1150 C product 19.2 % (Table 1 values are shifted one row down in the PDF text extraction; mapping fixed by the prose, lines 116-124).

r4_derived_printed.source: FINAL-PLAN.md §4.2 and r4-materials-scale.md (derived from the cited primary laws), checked at printed precision

plan_estimates_superseded.source: FINAL-PLAN.md §7 S1.5: "refuse any material with mu_code > 3.3 ... FTCS-analogue explicit estimate [DERIVED-r2/r5; its constant for the MLS stencil is UNVERIFIED]". Not an owner decision; superseded in the S1.5 review by the bound derived from the kernels (liquidGate.MPM_MU_CODE_LIMIT).

phase_bounds._about: Cited phase-change temperatures the code must carry exactly (copy integrity).

water_liquid_C_at_0p101325MPa.source: NIST WebBook SRD 69 isobar: first liquid row (triple-point temperature) and saturated-liquid row

ethanol_K.source: Sotiriadou et al. 2023 Eq. 13 validity: triple point 159 K to the 0.1 MPa boiling temperature 351.57 K

glycerol_boil_K.source: NIST WebBook: average of 6 values, 550 +- 40 K

iron_melt_K.source: NIST WebBook condensed-phase Shomate fits (JANAF): solid to 1809 K, liquid from 1809 K

salt_melt_K.source: NIST WebBook condensed-phase Shomate fits (JANAF): liquid NaCl from 1074 K

copper_freeze_K.source: ITS-90 defining fixed point, freezing point of copper T90 = 1357.77 K (Preston-Thomas 1990, Metrologia 27:3, Table 1; transcription at its-90.com)

sotiriadou2023_table7_0p1MPa.source: Sotiriadou et al. 2023, Int. J. Thermophys. 44:40, Table 7: ethanol at 0.1 MPa from the FULL correlation (Eq. 1, 8-12) and the reference EOS. Independent of Eq. 13 (the simplified 0.1 MPa correlation the code uses, stated 2.3 %) and of the CoolProp saturated-liquid density ancillary (stated max 0.737 % vs the EOS).
